# Build: token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-13T20:04:16.679Z
> list every token in a registry; any time a new UI is made add its tokens to the registry; an editor that takes whatever UI you pick and throws it in a sandbox with live preview, hot render as you edit; a default skin; every edit takes a snapshot, you see the chain of edits like a disk snapshot and can revert to any point; at any point export current to a new skin

## What to build
Continue build "Token registry and Skin Editor: live sandbox preview, snapshot history" (token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-13 20:04):
"list every token in a registry; any time a new UI is made add its tokens to the registry; an editor that takes whatever UI you pick and throws it in a sandbox with live preview, hot render as you edit; a default skin; every edit takes a snapshot, you see the chain of edits like a disk snapshot and can revert to any point; at any point export current to a new skin"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (5 left, ~50 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Runs after the token schema step of own-token-sets-for-grids-and-tab-groups (builds on its schema).
[ ] s2 (~10 min) TOKEN REGISTRY: one registry listing every token in the system, with element type, area (layout/style/colour/behaviour), state, light/dark, level (basic/pro/advanced), plain-English description, default and source. Every new UI, component or plugin MUST register its tokens through its manifest. A CI check fails any UI whose tokens aren't in the registry, and any registered token that nothing uses. Browsable and searchable, with full API.
[ ] s3 (~10 min) SKIN EDITOR (plugin and screen): pick any UI from the list (a screen, plugin, dialog, element), or pick it on screen, and it's loaded into a sandbox live-preview window with real components and sample data. Every edit hot-renders the preview in real time. The token list comes from the registry, with Basic/Pro/Advanced views. Inline element and asset editors work inside it.
[ ] s4 (~10 min) Full API: REST/MCP/CLI/voice ('revert the skin to 10 minutes ago', 'export this as a new skin called Midnight'). Tests, help, Shipped features. Fable for the registry and snapshot schema.
[ ] s5 (~10 min) list every token in a registry; any time a new UI is made add its tokens to the registry; an editor that takes whatever UI you pick and throws it in a sandbox with live preview, hot render as you edit; a default skin; every edit takes a snapshot, you see the chain of edits like a disk snapshot and can revert to any point; at any point export current to a new skin
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

list every token in a registry; any time a new UI is made add its tokens to the registry; an editor that takes whatever UI you pick and throws it in a sandbox with live preview, hot render as you edit; a default skin; every edit takes a snapshot, you see the chain of edits like a disk snapshot and can revert to any point; at any point export current to a new skin
DEFAULT SKIN: there is always a built-in default skin that is locked.

SNAPSHOTS: every edit to a skin automatically takes a snapshot (like a disk snapshot). A timeline shows the chain of edits, each with time, who/what made it, and a diff of exactly which tokens changed (old -> new). Click any snapshot to preview it, compare any two, or revert to it (a revert is itself a new snapshot, so nothing is ever lost). No breaking skins into separate style or colour groups: the skin is the only unit.
EXPORT: at any point, 'Export current to new skin' saves the current state as a brand-new skin (name, thumbnail, to the hub library).
Restore previous edit / Restore from axHub work through the snapshots.
Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/token-registry-skin-editor-live-sandbox.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR
